content: Do not pour this medication down the drain or flush it down the toilet unless specifically instructed to do so. Dispose of this product properly when it is expired or no longer needed. Medical Alert: Your medical condition may lead to complications during a medical emergency. Ensure that healthcare providers are aware of your condition. Important Information Usage: This document provides a summary and does not include all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for your specific situation. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete details about this product and your individual health needs. Uses: This medication contains glucagon, a natural hormone that raises blood sugar levels by prompting the liver to release stored sugar. It is used to treat severe hypoglycemia (very low blood sugar) that may require assistance from others. Additionally, glucagon may be administered before certain gastrointestinal X-ray procedures. How to Use: Read the Patient Information Leaflet and Instructions for Use provided by your pharmacist when you receive this medication and with each refill. Keep this medication accessible in case of an emergency. Caregivers should be familiar with the symptoms of low blood sugar (refer to the Precautions section) and trained on how to administer glucagon if necessary. Before using, visually inspect the product for particles or discoloration. Do not use the liquid if either is present. Administer this medication via injection into a muscle or under the skin as directed by your doctor. Dosage is determined based on age, and for children, it is also based on weight. If the individual is unconscious, turn them onto their side to prevent choking in case of vomiting. Once the person regains consciousness and can swallow, provide a quick source of sugar, such as glucose tablets or juice. Glucagon’s effects are temporary, and low blood sugar may recur. Contact your doctor immediately after an episode of severe hypoglycemia. Side Effects: Common side effects may include nausea, vomiting, or headache. Irritation, redness, or swelling at the injection site may also occur. Remember, this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Severe allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a comprehensive list of side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for guidance on side effects. Precautions: Before using glucagon, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients (e.g., latex in some products) that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Low blood sugar (hypoglycemia) is more likely if you do not consume enough calories or engage in unusually strenuous exercise. Symptoms of hypoglycemia include sudden sweating, shaking, rapid heartbeat, hunger, blurred vision, dizziness, or tingling in the hands or feet. It is advisable to carry glucose tablets or gel to treat low blood sugar. If these are unavailable, quickly raise your blood sugar by consuming a fast-acting sugar source, such as sugar, honey, candy, fruit juice, or non-diet soda. Notify your doctor immediately about the reaction and the use of this product. To prevent low blood sugar, eat meals on a regular schedule and avoid skipping meals. It is unknown if this drug passes into breast milk, but it is unlikely to harm a nursing infant. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all products you use (including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products) and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Overdose: In the event of an overdose with serious symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Storage: Different brands of this medication may have different storage requirements. Refer to the product packaging for specific storage instructions or consult your pharmacist. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Medical Alert: Your condition may lead to complications during a medical emergency. Ensure that healthcare providers are informed of your condition. Last Revised: August 2024.
